pnpm.//: Transitive advisories from `pnpm audit`, forced to their patched versions so the CI audit can be blocking instead of `|| true` - a non-blocking audit is a notification nobody reads. Each is a dependency of `next` or `eslint` that they pin below the fix. Every range is CAPPED TO ONE MAJOR on purpose: the first attempt wrote `>=1.1.17`, pnpm resolved brace-expansion to 5.0.8, and eslint died repo-wide with `TypeError: expand is not a function` because minimatch@3 wants the 1.x export shape. An override is a version pin, not a request for the newest thing that satisfies an inequality. Remove an entry once its parent ships a release that no longer needs it - `pnpm why <pkg>` shows whether it is still doing anything.
